title: Derived pro-etale direct image commutes with restriction of scalars
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and $\varphi:A\to B$ a homomorphism of finite commutative rings. For $W\in\{X,Y\}$ let $\varphi_W:A_W\to B_W$ be the induced map of constant sheaves of rings on the small pro-etale site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:\Sh(W_{\mathrm{proet}},B)\to\Sh(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be restriction of scalars along $\varphi_W$. It is exact, so applying it termwise defines a triangulated functor $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},B)\to D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. Let

$$
 Rf_*^{A}:D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A),\qquad
 Rf_*^{B}:D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},B)
$$

be the derived direct images defined with K-injective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Then there is an isomorphism of functors $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$

$$
 Rf_*^{A}\circ\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\circ Rf_*^{B},
$$

natural in the argument; for a K-injective complex $J$ of $B_X$-modules and a K-injective resolution $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi J\to I$ over $A_X$, its value is the inverse of the map $f_*\operatorname{Res}_\varphi J=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi f_*J\to f_*I$.

proof.text: Present ordinary A-module sheaves as modules over the sheafified constant ring. Restrict a ring-sheaf module along the constant-presheaf sheafification unit and read it as an A-module-valued sheaf. The realization equivalence of def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules and the sheafification adjunction unit give an equivalence in this direction as well. Its inverse preserves K-injective complexes and quasi-isomorphisms. The sheafification unit is locally bijective; the proof checks its underlying abelian presheaf explicitly, without choosing arbitrary module data.

proof.text: Take the constant commutative ring sheaves associated to A and B. Their coefficient map comes from the constant-sheaf functor. Naturality of the sheafification unit identifies its action on constants with phi. The canonical constant-ring inverse-image map is an isomorphism for finite discrete rings by prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact. The direct-image structural map is its adjoint; the adjunction and sheafification hom-equivalences show that it preserves the prescribed constant sections. Consequently the scalar-model equivalences intertwine restriction of scalars and direct image by identity-on-elements natural isomorphisms, with linearity proved from these two unit equations.

proof.text: For a K-injective B-module complex I and a K-injective resolution j of its A-restriction, transport I, its restriction and j through the inverse scalar-model equivalences. Apply the ringed-module restriction_directImage_quasiIso consequence of lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction, itself using the resolution clause of the unbounded ringed-topos composition theorem. The intertwining natural isomorphisms and invariance of quasi-isomorphisms under equivalences give that ordinary A-direct-image(j) is a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of the right-derived unit at j now makes that unit invertible on the restriction of I. This does not assert that restriction preserves K-injectivity.

The underived pullback/restriction square has identity direct-image mate by the restriction/coextension triangle identity. Transport the derived adjunction along the canonical left-derived/map-derived-category identification. The generic derived_mate_factors equation expresses the named mate through the two right-derived units. On a K-injective B-complex, the B-unit and the A-unit of step 3 are isomorphisms; cancel the other exact-functor comparison isomorphisms to deduce that the named mate is invertible. Every derived object has a K-injective representative, so naturality gives invertibility everywhere. The unchanged forward comparison is the inverse of this mate. Finally, unit naturality at j and cancellation of the K-injective units prove the published normalization equality, while the quasi-isomorphism conjunct reuses the transported resolution clause of step 3.
